subject: Logs evidence packaging & RFI — next steps and deliverables
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam Peterson <liam.peterson@supplytech.com>, security@supplitech.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Logs evidence packaging & RFI — next steps and deliverables

Hi Liam / team,

Great to meet you earlier — thanks for walking through your compliance requirements. Below is a concise recap from our side plus suggested deliverables so you can move the RFI/RFP and internal review forward.

Quick recap of Redwood logging capabilities (high level):
- Admin activity logs: captures actor (user/service), action verb, target resource, timestamp (UTC), IP, request_id, and any role-change details.
- API request logs: request metadata (path, method, headers), response status, latency, a stable request_id and optional request/response body hashes (we redact full PII by default).
- Exportability: ad-hoc and scheduled exports in NDJSON or compressed CSV; exports include signed manifests and checksums.
- Retention & immutability: default retention windows are configurable per-tenant. For immutable evidence we provide an export workflow that writes to customer-owned object stores with signed manifests and a manifest-level content hash for chain-of-custody.
- SOC 2 / compliance posture: SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress; control evidence for infra and change management is available today. Expected finalization: August 2027 (target).
- GDPR/HIPAA notes: data residency controls available for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted API has data processing addenda and supports standard GDPR contractual terms. We currently support BAA for Private deployments — happy to scope hosted options if required.

Items we can deliver (what would be most useful to you):
1) Redacted sample NDJSON export (7–14 days of activity) with a readme describing fields and hashes.
2) A short tech brief describing our immutability/export workflow (WORM options, manifest format, verification steps) — PDF.
3) SOC 2 status and a list of available evidence artifacts (control IDs we can map to questionnaire items).
4) Suggested minimal retention/collection config to satisfy your e-discovery needs and recommended retention values.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm which items (1–4) you'd like us to prioritize.
- Any required export format (NDJSON vs CSV), retention horizon target (e.g., 1 year vs 7 years), and whether you need exports to land in a SupplyTech-owned S3 bucket.
- Specific chain-of-custody requirements (signed manifests, timestamp authority, notarization) if you have them.

Attached: redwood-log-export-spec.pdf — contains field mappings and an example manifest.

Would you prefer we push the NDJSON sample first, or the SOC 2 / evidence list? I can have the sample ready within 48 hours once you confirm scope.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-log-export-spec.pdf (12KB) — field mapping and manifest example
From: Liam Peterson <liam.peterson@supplytech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, security@supplitech.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logs evidence packaging & RFI — next steps and deliverables

Jordan, thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our security team so we can route the RFI internally: 

- Export format: NDJSON preferred.
- Retention horizon: regulatory requirement drives 7 years for some records; for initial evaluation we'd like a 1-year export sample plus a clear path to 7+ year retention.
- Immutability proof: we need a description of the chain-of-custody process and a verification procedure we can run (hashes + signed manifest is a good start). Do you support timestamp-authority-signed manifests or an equivalent?
- SOC 2: could you provide the current SOC 2 letter for infra and the list of available artifacts we can request (changes, access reviews, incident logs)?
- HIPAA: confirm whether hosted API is eligible for BAA or if that is only for Private/Dedicated deployments.

I've attached our security questionnaire with the baseline items — some are marked high priority. If you can populate the spreadsheet (or point us to the evidence artifacts) that will speed our procurement review.

Also, timeline: we have a procurement checkpoint next Wednesday (26 May). Ideally we get the NDJSON sample and the SOC 2 evidence list before then.

Thanks — Liam
Liam Peterson
Security Programs, SupplyTech
liam.peterson@supplytech.com | +1 (503) 555-0122
